title: Free topple: the sim's pendulum is RIGHT (lambda 7.46 vs 7.74 locked) -- inertia is not the lag-fragility
question: Is the sim plant's pendulum time constant wrong (box-model inertia from the measured 5 cm com), and is that why the filtered classical stands on hardware but falls in sim (run 28, reconfirmed after run 35)?
headline: 8 topples, motors coasting: wheels stayed stiction-locked (roll +-1-2 deg), lambda = 7.46 +- 0.3 1/s by the energy fit (omega^2 vs cos theta). Replicating the identical experiment in sim -- locked drivetrain via wheel-joint frictionloss -- gives 7.74, a 4% match; the sim's t(2->45 deg) of 560 ms sits inside the real 440-575 ms spread. So the box model's inertia is fine and the com suspect is RULED OUT: the free-wheel plant (lambda 11.7) vs locked plant (7.5) split was the earlier confusion. Follow-up single-parameter fixes for the lag-fragility all REFUTED in sim: wheel-joint stiction 0.05-0.2 N*m (still falls), reduced delay (5 ms already kills it at any stiction; hardware stands with ~19 ms), pitch damping as a tire-patch proxy (helps only at an implausible 40% of critical, at 80% mean duty). The sim-real mismatch is structural and multi-dimensional -> switch from one-suspect-at-a-time to a joint multi-probe fit.
